name: Presentation (16:9)
note: Two kinds of slides. (1) Reference slides designed by the brand team in Figma (Design MCP › Layouts): kept as designed; only background colour, fonts, chips and logo placement are mapped to the design system. (2) Slides Claude designs: follow every guardrail below. Approved 2026-10-16.

hero_title.use: page breaker and closing statements, big numbers

eyebrow.use: kicker above the headline, case as written (uppercase optional)

panel_heading.use: panel heading, case as written (uppercase optional)

chip.use: label chips, case as written (uppercase optional)

guardrails.note: Guidance for whoever designs in this format. user_decides = what is made (the user's call); fixed = do not change; must_not = hard limits; avoid = strong advice; design_direction = how to use the system; claude_decides = how it looks, where the designer has freedom. Every design item cites its basis in the design system.
user_decides: What is being made, for whom and why: the deck, its purpose and audience.
The content and facts. The designer uses exactly what the user supplies or approves: never invents, adds, rewrites, shortens or cuts it, and asks before suggesting a change.
The scope: which slides; nothing is added that was not asked for; when it is unclear, ask.
The number of slides, when the user sets it.
Whether AI slides are dark (Claude asks; there is no default).
Which page-breaker or closing design to use, from the reference slides.

fixed.text: 52px padding on all four sides (spacing/52) on every slide, hero slides included: logo, labels, titles and content all align to it; content area 1816 × 976 px.
Text uses the named text style for its element (e.g. headline Display/LG Bold, body Body/24), between 14px and 72px.
Logo top-right on the 52px edge: white on dark and brand slides, blue on light; size may vary.
Delivered as an HTML file. HTML is the only export.
Three themes: light (background/primary), dark (background/inverse) and brand (background/brand), each with its fixed text and logo colours.
Reference slides from Figma keep their design; only background colour, fonts, chips and logo placement are mapped to the design system.

claude_decides: Layout and composition within the grid: what goes where, how many columns, what leads.
Visual hierarchy: what is large, what is quiet, and how the eye moves.
Which components to use and how to combine them, and new card designs on Card base when the named cards don't fit the content.
How to show each idea: a stat, a process, a comparison, a story.
How the requested content is spread across slides (unless the user sets the number), and the single message of each slide.

overrides.reason: Matches the brand team's designed slides (small text and chart labels at 14px and up); decided 2026-10-16.

logo.note: Top-right on the 52px edge by default; another corner only when the slide design needs it (for example a tab row across the top).

dark.note: Mapped from the designed slides' #132335 to the nearest token.

ai_slides.rule: AI slides have no default theme. Ask the user whether they want them dark; otherwise pick the theme for the slide like any other (decision ai-slides-theme-optional, 2026-10-28).

content_forms.rule: Before designing a slide, name the shape of its content and draw it in the matching form, built from design-system parts and the blocks (Process flow, Stat tile, Comparison table, Feature grid). A grid or row of text cards is only for like items that sit side by side (decision infographic-required).
content_forms.references: get_brand_guidelines(section: "data-viz"): reference layouts for numbers, steps, stages, cycles and systems (stat layouts, charts, funnel, flywheel, staircase, plant drawings), the same in every format. References, not fixed layouts: build designs like them, adapted to the content.

forms.sequence: Steps, a workflow or a ticket flow in order: a flow or timeline with numbered nodes and connectors (Process flow), short text under each node.
forms.lifecycle: A cycle that repeats (MLOps, closed loop, detect-act-verify-learn): a loop diagram, the stages placed around a circle or closed path with arrows back to the start.
forms.phases: Phases or a roadmap over time: a timeline or growing phase blocks along one axis.
forms.problem_solution: A problem and its answer, or before and after: a split contrast, the problem side in the Negative intent and the answer in brand or Positive.
forms.numbers: Numbers, results and KPIs: big numbers, stat rows (Stat tile) or a chart.
forms.comparison: Options or features compared: a comparison table or matrix (Comparison table).
forms.architecture: Systems, data flow or integration: an architecture diagram in the architecture format's language (see architecture_slides).
forms.like_items: Parallel items of the same kind (capabilities, tools, objectives): a grid with a Lucide icon per item (Feature grid), cards sized to their content.
forms.people: A team: the team reference slide or template, with headshots from the asset library where they exist.

architecture_slides.rule: Any slide showing a system architecture, data flow or integration follows the architecture format: call get_brand_guidelines(section: "rules", format_profile: "architecture") and use its zones, node styles (boxed tag, tag, label, caption), icons from the architecture icon library, arrows and colours, and the I/O Sense outcome when the diagram ends in I/O Sense. Start from the architecture templates. Scale it into the slide's content area; deck text stays at 14px or more (decision architecture-in-decks).

product_slides.rule: Slides about what a product shows (an I/O Sense screen, a dashboard, an operator view) use the light theme and show the product as a dashboard mockup next to the user's points (decision product-slides-light-with-mockup).
product_slides.mockup_placeholder: Until product screenshots are in the asset library, place a placeholder frame where the mockup goes, at the size and position the design needs: container/secondary, 1px dashed border/strong, radius/3xl, with the label DASHBOARD_MOCKUP_<NAME> centred in Body/24 text/secondary. Never draw a fake product UI. List every placeholder in the delivery note so the user can drop in the screenshot.

icons.note: Sizes in px at the design size. In a UI card the icon square follows the card: pick the step for the card's width, so a bigger card gets a bigger icon and square (CSS container queries on the card). The square is the icon plus 8px (gap/inline) on every side, a solid fill with no border; square only. Figma: the Icon square component (Size = icon size).
